title: On-Delay Timers -- Where AB and Siemens DIVERGE
concept:
Timers are the #1 place Allen-Bradley and Siemens Structured Text look
different -- a favorite interview topic, so learn both.

An ON-DELAY timer waits a set time after its input goes TRUE before its output
turns on. Real example: after the operator presses Run (Run_Cmd), delay 5
seconds -- warning horn / lube prelube -- then energize Motor_Run.

You'll implement the 5-second on-delay in EITHER vendor's style; the checker
accepts both.
ab_note:
IMPORTANT: Studio 5000 ST does NOT support the plain TON/TOF/RTO you know from
ladder. In ST you use the RESET variants -- TONR, TOFR, RTOR -- and the timer
tag must be type FBD_TIMER (not TIMER). Preset .PRE and accumulator .ACC are in
MILLISECONDS.

    Start_Dly.PRE := 5000;               // 5 s, in ms
    Start_Dly.TimerEnable := Run_Cmd;
    TONR(Start_Dly);
    Motor_Run := Start_Dly.DN;           // .DN = done bit
siemens_note:
TIA Portal / SCL uses the IEC timers TON, TOF, TP as function blocks, each
needing an instance data block. Presets use TIME literals (T#5s, T#500ms).

    "IEC_Timer_0_DB".TON(IN := Run_Cmd,
                         PT := T#5s,          // preset time
                         Q  => Motor_Run);    // output
task:
Energize Motor_Run 5 seconds after Run_Cmd turns on. Write a 5-second on-delay
in EITHER style:

    Allen-Bradley:  TONR(...) with a 5000 ms preset, then drive Motor_Run from
                    the timer's .DN bit.
    Siemens SCL:    TON(...) with PT := T#5s and send Q => Motor_Run.

The checker accepts either vendor's syntax.
starter:
(* Lesson 04 -- On-Delay Timers: where Allen-Bradley and Siemens DIVERGE *)

VAR
    Run_Cmd   : BOOL;   (* N.O. run command -> XIC (as-is)   *)
    Motor_Run : BOOL;   (* output: follows Run_Cmd by 5 s    *)
    Start_Dly : TONR;   (* AB on-delay timer instance        *)
    (* Siemens equivalent lives in an IEC TON instance DB (IEC_Timer_0_DB) *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
    (* TODO: 5-second on-delay so Motor_Run turns on 5 s after Run_Cmd.
       Pick ONE vendor style below (Allen-Bradley TONR or Siemens TON). *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

checks.message: Calls an on-delay timer (TONR for AB, TON for Siemens)
checks.hint: Studio 5000 ST uses TONR(...); Siemens SCL uses TON(...).

checks.message: Sets a 5-second preset (5000 ms in Studio 5000, or T#5s in SCL)
Drives Motor_Run from the timer output (.DN in AB, Q in Siemens)
checks.hint: AB: Motor_Run := Start_Dly.DN;   Siemens: pass  Q => Motor_Run  in the call.

solution:
(* Lesson 04 -- On-Delay Timers: where Allen-Bradley and Siemens DIVERGE *)

VAR
    Run_Cmd   : BOOL;   (* N.O. run command -> XIC (as-is)   *)
    Motor_Run : BOOL;   (* output: follows Run_Cmd by 5 s    *)
    Start_Dly : TONR;   (* AB on-delay timer instance        *)
    (* Siemens equivalent lives in an IEC TON instance DB (IEC_Timer_0_DB) *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
    (* --- Allen-Bradley (Studio 5000) --- *)
    Start_Dly.PRE := 5000;                // 5 seconds, in ms
    Start_Dly.TimerEnable := Run_Cmd;
    TONR(Start_Dly);
    Motor_Run := Start_Dly.DN;

    (* --- Siemens (TIA Portal / SCL) --- *)
    "IEC_Timer_0_DB".TON(IN := Run_Cmd,
                         PT := T#5s,
                         Q  => Motor_Run);
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
